solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fix outside of broken boat: get fuel here

indicators.note: the fixing word sits outside, wrapped around the rest

parts.note: to fix something in place is to peg it

indicators.note: a broken boat has its letters smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone mending the shell of a wrecked boat, and a refuelling stop.
explanation.walkthrough: Peat, cut and dried, is burned as fuel, so the definition describes the place rather than naming it.
explanation.definitionFit: Peat is dug from boggy ground and dried for burning, so a peat bog is where that fuel is obtained.

clue.text: Expressed full agreement

indicators.note: expressed means said aloud, so we want a word that sounds the same

parts.note: packed means full

explanation.surface: Voicing complete assent.
explanation.definitionFit: A pact is a formal agreement or treaty.

clue.text: Criticises a revenue-raising measure on radio

indicators.note: on the radio we only hear words, so their sound is what matters

parts.note: a tax raises revenue for government, so this is a plus tax, said together

explanation.surface: A broadcaster slates a new tax.
explanation.definitionFit: To attack an idea is to criticise it strongly.

clue.text: One gripping beer half-heartedly

indicators.note: the heart of the beer word is a pair of identical letters; half of it goes

parts.note: bitter is a British style of draught beer

explanation.surface: Someone holding a beer without much enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: A biter is something that bites, clamping its teeth or jaws.

clue.text: Grey not satisfied with girl's embrace

indicators.note: the girl's embrace wraps around the other word

parts.note: gal is a girl; the 's makes her the one embracing
unmet demands are not satisfied

explanation.surface: A disappointed lover in a girl's arms, looking glum.
explanation.definitionFit: Gunmetal is a dull bluish-grey colour, named after the alloy.

clue.text: Depraved Republican's off to arouse a Liberal

indicators.note: the Republican is off, that is, leaves the word for rousing

parts.note: to bestir is to rouse or stir into action
Republican's reads as Republican is; R is the abbreviation

explanation.surface: A political scandal: a degenerate Republican sets out to excite a Liberal.
explanation.definitionFit: Bestial behaviour is brutish and beastlike, hence morally depraved.

clue.text: Muscle oil giant's keeping in reserve

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside

parts.note: BP is the oil company; the 's adds its S
something on ice is kept in reserve

explanation.surface: An oil company holding something back for later.
explanation.definitionFit: The biceps is the large muscle at the front of the upper arm.

clue.text: Brilliance of older puns lost

indicators.note: letters that are lost have strayed out of their places into a new order

explanation.surface: Old wordplay has lost its sparkle.
explanation.definitionFit: Splendour is magnificence, a dazzling brightness or grandeur.

clue.text: Knew reworked Breaking Bad as resource for writer to draw on

definitions.text: resource for writer to draw on

indicators.note: the rearranged word breaks into the middle of the other one

parts.note: ill means bad, as in ill health

indicators.note: reworked means the letters of knew are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A writer reworking a TV hit, Breaking Bad, as source material.
explanation.walkthrough: Breaking Bad is the TV drama; here the title splits into an indicator and a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: An inkwell holds ink from which a pen-wielding writer would literally draw.

clue.text: Why tangles developed between ends?

indicators.note: developed means the letters are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about how knots form.
explanation.definitionFit: Lengthways means along the length, running from one end to the other.

clue.text: Unresponsive pet given a pick-me-up

parts.note: a cat is a typical pet
a tonic is a restorative drink or medicine

explanation.surface: A listless pet animal is given a restorative.
explanation.walkthrough: The tonic is ironic: a catatonic creature is beyond being picked up.
explanation.definitionFit: A catatonic person is in a stupor, not reacting to stimuli.

clue.text: Compare plant on rocks to some ears?

indicators.note: some people say lichen exactly like the answer, so the sound is what counts

parts.note: lichen grows as a crust on rocks and walls

explanation.surface: Asking whether a rock plant might be likened to ears.
explanation.walkthrough: LICHEN has two pronunciations, 'litchen' and 'lyken'; only the second gives the answer, hence 'some ears'.
explanation.definitionFit: To liken one thing to another is to draw a comparison between them.

clue.text: Journalist runs into alleged adulterer

indicators.note: the runs letter goes into the other word

parts.note: in a divorce, the co-respondent is the person accused of adultery with the spouse

explanation.surface: A reporter bumps into someone named in a divorce case.
explanation.walkthrough: R for runs comes from cricket scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: A correspondent is a reporter covering a particular subject or place for a paper.

clue.text: Legal details of right in case of short measure …

indicators.note: the second word acts as a case enclosing the right letter

parts.note: a small pint is a pint glass short of beer

explanation.surface: Legal fine points on your rights when served short measure.
explanation.definitionFit: Small print is the terms and conditions in tiny type, the legal fine detail.

clue.text: Wind around island makes for poor hearing

indicators.note: the wind goes around the island letter

parts.note: the mistral is a cold northerly wind of southern France

explanation.surface: A gale blowing round an island makes it hard to hear anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearing' is the legal kind, not the ear's.
explanation.definitionFit: A mistrial is a trial rendered invalid by an error, so a court hearing that went wrong.

clue.text: … reason being to restrict supply of beer

parts.note: to ration is to limit how much is supplied
ale is beer

explanation.surface: Continuing 12: the justification is to limit beer, the short measure.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the reasoning behind a decision.

clue.text: Capital transfixed by leaders of general workers in industrial action

indicators.note: the capital is pierced through by the letters on either side
the leaders of words are their first letters

parts.note: the first letters of general and workers
Oslo is the capital of Norway

explanation.surface: A capital city gripped by union leaders during a dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: A go-slow is a protest in which workers deliberately work slowly instead of striking.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-slow is a form of protest by employees, a kind of strike tactic.

clue.text: Fetching gift from cleaner's mother

parts.note: a char is a cleaning lady; the 's reads as is
ma is mother

explanation.surface: A charming present from the cleaning lady's mum.
explanation.walkthrough: A char, or charwoman, is a British term for a woman hired to clean.
explanation.definitionFit: Charisma is an attractive personal quality, a natural gift for charming people.

clue.text: Native American western at famous corral on location in California

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another comes after it

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles

indicators.note: in an across answer, going west means reading right to left

parts.note: the OK Corral at Tombstone, scene of the famous gunfight

explanation.surface: A Western film shot on location in California about the OK Corral gunfight.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lakota are a Sioux people of the Great Plains.

clue.text: Dog and mink scrapping for territory

indicators.note: scrapping here means fighting, so the two animals' letters tumble together

explanation.surface: Two animals fighting over their patch.
explanation.definitionFit: A kingdom is a realm, the territory ruled by a monarch.

clue.text: Drug dealer using speed sustains damage

indicators.note: to sustain is to hold up, so one word holds the other within it

parts.note: pacy means fast, moving with speed
harm is damage

explanation.surface: A pusher on amphetamines does harm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drug dealer' and 'speed' suggest the street; the dealer is a legitimate chemist's shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A pharmacy is a shop that dispenses medicines, so a legitimate seller of drugs.

clue.text: I agree, shame when leader's lacking pleasant disposition

parts.note: amen is said to express agreement

indicators.note: the word's leader, its first letter, is missing

parts.note: 'what a shame' is 'what a pity'

explanation.surface: Agreeing that it's a pity when leadership is absent.
explanation.definitionFit: Amenity in its older sense is pleasantness of manner or setting.

clue.text: Popular Muslim ruler seeing off an attack

parts.note: in means popular, fashionable

indicators.note: to see off is to get rid of, so those letters go

parts.note: a sultan is a Muslim sovereign

explanation.surface: A well-liked sultan repels an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: An insult is a verbal attack, an offensive remark.

clue.text: Crossing one game with another

parts.note: pontoon is a card game, the British name for blackjack or twenty-one
bridge is another card game

explanation.surface: Mixing one game with another.
explanation.definitionFit: A pontoon bridge is a temporary crossing laid on floating supports.

clue.text: Repeat song endlessly: nothing can end it

indicators.note: the nothing letter goes on the end
endlessly means the song word is cut short, without its end, so its final letter goes

parts.note: a ditty is a short simple song

explanation.surface: Instructions for an annoying tune played on a loop.
explanation.definitionFit: Ditto means the same again, used to show something is repeated.

clue.text: It's no go for tech firm to survey inappropriately

indicators.note: no go means the go letters are dropped from the firm's name

parts.note: Google is the search-engine company

explanation.surface: A tech company is barred from snooping on people.
explanation.definitionFit: To ogle is to stare lecherously, looking at someone in an improper way.

clue.text: Making call, I land

definitions.meaning: The radio call word for the letter I in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.walkthrough: The NATO phonetic alphabet gives each letter a word: Alpha, Bravo ... India for I.
explanation.definitionFit: The country also serves as the radio code word spelled out for the letter I.

clue.text: Traumatic to increase crossword output?

parts.note: to up a price is to raise it
setting is what a crossword compiler, the setter, does

explanation.surface: A setter is asked to produce more puzzles, which proves distressing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something upsetting causes distress, as a traumatic event does.

clue.text: Art working for a while perhaps to create a storm?

parts.note: to temp is to work in a temporary job
art is the archaic second person of be; old verbs for thou end in -est, as in thou goest

explanation.surface: An artist's temporary job stirs up trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'thou tempest': in archaic English that means 'thou art temping', so 'Art working for a while' gives the answer; the play also has Prospero's art raising a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: A tempest is a violent storm, as in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: Follower found back in society locale

indicators.note: back means the run of letters is read backwards
in means the answer lies within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the words society and locale

explanation.surface: A disciple discovered in a fashionable venue.
explanation.definitionFit: An acolyte is an assistant or devoted adherent of a leader.
